publication.banner: Public research study · original and complex-query results verified

study.title: Does GPU-accelerated Spark beat Polars?
study.subtitle: A fixed-configuration, single-host experiment from 6 million to 1.8 billion line items.

hardware.label: CPU allocation
hardware.value: 30-vCPU AMD EPYC 7J13 host; Spark local[30], Polars pool 30

hardware.label: Host memory
hardware.value: Approximately 216 GiB RAM; Spark driver heap 96 GiB

limitations: Six selected original queries, with four join queries already present; this is not a complete or certified TPC-H result.
Scores sum six per-query medians. They are not once-through suite runtimes or physical throughput measurements of the full 108 GB dataset.
One recorded warmup and three measured trials within one engine session per scale; descriptive ranges, not independent statistical experiments.
Filesystem preheating is attempted before each engine; residency is not guaranteed. No application DataFrame cache is used. Startup is excluded from query medians.
Monetary and quantity inputs use Float64/DOUBLE. Outputs are tolerance-checked against saved Polars warmups; these are not independent full-scale oracle proofs.
A single A100 host with different native memory budgets does not establish distributed scaling, equivalent-cost performance, energy use, or a universal product winner.
Final-plan operator names show selected GPU, hybrid, or CPU-fallback work; they do not measure runtime fractions. The complex suite remains separate from the original score.

The revised complex suite observes explicit cleanup outside each query timer. Garbage collection can affect the next query's heap state; all displayed complex cases use one uniform protocol, separate from the earlier attempt. Cleanup totals over warmup plus three actions cannot be added to a sum of medians to estimate end-to-end time.
This study is publicly accessible. Review the included notices before redistributing code or adapted workload definitions.

original.label: Original six queries
original.status_text: Verified observations at five scales; no overall GPU-plugin Spark win was observed on this six-query workload.

queries.description: Broad scan, arithmetic, and grouped aggregates
queries.sql:
SELECT l_returnflag, l_linestatus,
            SUM(l_quantity) AS sum_qty,
            SUM(l_extendedprice) AS sum_base_price,
            SUM(l_extendedprice * (1 - l_discount)) AS sum_disc_price,
            SUM(l_extendedprice * (1 - l_discount) * (1 + l_tax)) AS sum_charge,
            AVG(l_quantity) AS avg_qty,
            AVG(l_extendedprice) AS avg_price,
            AVG(l_discount) AS avg_disc,
            COUNT(*) AS count_order
        FROM lineitem
        WHERE l_shipdate <= DATE '1998-09-02'
        GROUP BY l_returnflag, l_linestatus
        ORDER BY l_returnflag, l_linestatus

queries.description: Selective three-table join, aggregation, and top 10
queries.sql:
SELECT l_orderkey,
            SUM(l_extendedprice * (1 - l_discount)) AS revenue,
            o_orderdate, o_shippriority
        FROM lineitem
        JOIN orders ON l_orderkey = o_orderkey
        JOIN customer ON o_custkey = c_custkey
        WHERE c_mktsegment = 'BUILDING'
            AND o_orderdate < DATE '1995-03-15'
            AND l_shipdate > DATE '1995-03-15'
        GROUP BY l_orderkey, o_orderdate, o_shippriority
        ORDER BY revenue DESC, o_orderdate, l_orderkey, o_shippriority
        LIMIT 10

queries.description: Selective scan and scalar revenue aggregation
queries.sql:
SELECT SUM(l_extendedprice * l_discount) AS revenue
        FROM lineitem
        WHERE l_shipdate >= DATE '1994-01-01'
            AND l_shipdate < DATE '1995-01-01'
            AND l_discount BETWEEN 0.05 AND 0.07
            AND l_quantity < 24

queries.description: Four-table join, customer aggregation, and top 20
queries.sql:
SELECT c_custkey, c_name,
            SUM(l_extendedprice * (1 - l_discount)) AS revenue,
            c_acctbal, n_name, c_address, c_phone, c_comment
        FROM customer
        JOIN orders ON c_custkey = o_custkey
        JOIN lineitem ON o_orderkey = l_orderkey
        JOIN nation ON c_nationkey = n_nationkey
        WHERE o_orderdate >= DATE '1993-10-01'
            AND o_orderdate < DATE '1994-01-01'
            AND l_returnflag = 'R'
        GROUP BY c_custkey, c_name, c_acctbal, n_name,
            c_address, c_phone, c_comment
        ORDER BY revenue DESC, c_custkey
        LIMIT 20

SELECT l_shipmode,
            SUM(CASE WHEN o_orderpriority IN ('1-URGENT', '2-HIGH')
                THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS high_line_count,
            SUM(CASE WHEN o_orderpriority NOT IN ('1-URGENT', '2-HIGH')
                THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS low_line_count
        FROM lineitem
        JOIN orders ON l_orderkey = o_orderkey
        WHERE l_shipmode IN ('MAIL', 'SHIP')
            AND l_commitdate < l_receiptdate
            AND l_shipdate < l_commitdate
            AND l_receiptdate >= DATE '1994-01-01'
            AND l_receiptdate < DATE '1995-01-01'
        GROUP BY l_shipmode
        ORDER BY l_shipmode

queries.description: Part join and conditional revenue ratio
queries.sql:
SELECT 100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN p_type LIKE 'PROMO%'
            THEN l_extendedprice * (1 - l_discount) ELSE 0.0 END)
            / SUM(l_extendedprice * (1 - l_discount)) AS promo_revenue
        FROM lineitem
        JOIN part ON l_partkey = p_partkey
        WHERE l_shipdate >= DATE '1995-09-01'
            AND l_shipdate < DATE '1995-10-01'

queries.description: Six-table join with a composite partsupp key and profit by nation/year
queries.category: Six-table join and composite join keys
queries.sql:
SELECT nation, o_year, SUM(amount) AS sum_profit
        FROM (
            SELECT n_name AS nation, YEAR(o_orderdate) AS o_year,
                l_extendedprice * (1.0 - l_discount)
                    - ps_supplycost * l_quantity AS amount
            FROM lineitem
            JOIN part ON l_partkey = p_partkey
            JOIN supplier ON l_suppkey = s_suppkey
            JOIN partsupp ON l_partkey = ps_partkey AND l_suppkey = ps_suppkey
            JOIN orders ON l_orderkey = o_orderkey
            JOIN nation ON s_nationkey = n_nationkey
            WHERE p_name LIKE '%green%'
        ) AS profit
        GROUP BY nation, o_year
        ORDER BY nation, o_year DESC

queries.description: Left outer join and nested aggregation, including zero-order customers
queries.category: Left outer join and nested aggregation
queries.sql:
SELECT c_count, COUNT(*) AS custdist
        FROM (
            SELECT c_custkey, COUNT(o_orderkey) AS c_count
            FROM customer
            LEFT JOIN (
                SELECT o_custkey, o_orderkey
                FROM orders
                WHERE o_comment NOT LIKE '%special%requests%'
            ) AS eligible_orders ON c_custkey = o_custkey
            GROUP BY c_custkey
        ) AS customer_orders
        GROUP BY c_count
        ORDER BY custdist DESC, c_count DESC

SELECT c.c_custkey, c.c_name, c.c_nationkey
        FROM customer AS c
        WHERE EXISTS (
            SELECT 1
            FROM orders AS o
            WHERE o.o_custkey = c.c_custkey
                AND o.o_orderdate >= DATE '1995-01-01'
                AND o.o_orderdate < DATE '1996-01-01'
                AND EXISTS (
                    SELECT 1
                    FROM lineitem AS l
                    WHERE l.l_orderkey = o.o_orderkey
                        AND l.l_receiptdate > l.l_commitdate
                        AND l.l_shipmode IN ('AIR', 'SHIP')
                )
        )
        AND NOT EXISTS (
            SELECT 1
            FROM orders AS o
            WHERE o.o_custkey = c.c_custkey
                AND o.o_orderdate >= DATE '1996-01-01'
                AND o.o_orderdate < DATE '1997-01-01'
                AND o.o_orderstatus = 'F'
        )
        ORDER BY c.c_custkey
        LIMIT 100
queries.plan_note: The SQL expresses correlated EXISTS and NOT EXISTS conditions. Saved SF30/SF100 plans from the earlier v1 attempt removed the LeftAnti branch and retained two LeftSemi joins. This input design is not evidence of observed GPU anti-join execution; final plans determine the executed operator coverage.

queries.description: Two customer windows over 1994–1995 orders and top three per customer
queries.category: Two window orderings: LAG and ROW_NUMBER
queries.sql:
WITH windowed AS (
            SELECT o_custkey AS custkey, o_orderkey AS orderkey,
                o_orderdate AS orderdate, o_totalprice AS totalprice,
                LAG(o_totalprice) OVER (
                    PARTITION BY o_custkey
                    ORDER BY o_orderdate ASC NULLS LAST,
                        o_orderkey ASC NULLS LAST
                ) AS previous_totalprice,
                ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
                    PARTITION BY o_custkey
                    ORDER BY o_totalprice DESC NULLS LAST,
                        o_orderdate ASC NULLS LAST,
                        o_orderkey ASC NULLS LAST
                ) AS row_num
            FROM orders
            WHERE o_orderdate >= DATE '1994-01-01'
                AND o_orderdate < DATE '1996-01-01'
        )
        SELECT custkey, orderkey, orderdate, totalprice, previous_totalprice, row_num
        FROM windowed
        WHERE row_num <= 3
        ORDER BY custkey ASC NULLS LAST, row_num, orderkey ASC NULLS LAST
        LIMIT 100

queries.description: Four-table join with three exact distinct counts for 1995 orders
queries.category: Four-table join and three exact distinct counts
queries.sql:
SELECT n_name, o_orderpriority,
            COUNT(DISTINCT o_orderkey) AS distinct_orders,
            COUNT(DISTINCT o_custkey) AS distinct_customers,
            COUNT(DISTINCT l_partkey) AS distinct_parts
        FROM lineitem
        JOIN orders ON l_orderkey = o_orderkey
        JOIN supplier ON l_suppkey = s_suppkey
        JOIN nation ON s_nationkey = n_nationkey
        WHERE o_orderdate >= DATE '1995-01-01'
            AND o_orderdate < DATE '1996-01-01'
        GROUP BY n_name, o_orderpriority
        ORDER BY n_name ASC NULLS LAST, o_orderpriority ASC NULLS LAST

queries.description: 1994 lineitem equijoin with a residual line-number inequality
queries.category: Fact self-join with an inequality condition
queries.sql:
SELECT left_item.l_shipmode AS left_shipmode,
            right_item.l_shipmode AS right_shipmode,
            COUNT(*) AS pair_count
        FROM lineitem AS left_item
        JOIN lineitem AS right_item
            ON left_item.l_orderkey = right_item.l_orderkey
            AND left_item.l_linenumber < right_item.l_linenumber
        WHERE left_item.l_shipdate >= DATE '1994-01-01'
            AND left_item.l_shipdate < DATE '1995-01-01'
            AND right_item.l_shipdate >= DATE '1994-01-01'
            AND right_item.l_shipdate < DATE '1995-01-01'
        GROUP BY left_item.l_shipmode, right_item.l_shipmode
        ORDER BY left_shipmode ASC NULLS LAST, right_shipmode ASC NULLS LAST

protocol.label: Verified cleanup after every query
protocol.description: The revised complex suite requests Python garbage collection for Polars and Python/JVM garbage collection for Spark after each query returns. Spark then waits until the observed owned shuffle files and bytes are zero, outside the query timer.
protocol.timing_note: Explicit garbage collection may alter the next query's heap state. All displayed complex scales and engines use this same protocol; the earlier attempt is excluded. Query medians exclude cleanup, while process wall time includes it. Cleanup totals cover the warmup and all three measured actions: adding them to a sum of query medians would not produce an end-to-end runtime.

cleanup.scope: Session totals cover all saved warmup and measured barriers, including any cases excluded from the displayed performance comparison. Process wall time also includes startup, setup and other process overhead; it is not a cleanup-only measure.
